title: File-lock coordination service (advisory, TTL, fairness)
goal: An advisory file-lock service that arbitrates acquire/release/expire of locks by path_hmac with TTLs and first-come fairness, without ever seeing a path.
scope_in: Handler for file.lock frames (action acquire|release from clients; deny|expire emitted by the server) keyed by (sid, path_hmac).
TTL locks: default ttl_ms 60 000, min 1 000, max 600 000; renewal by re-acquire from the same agent extends the TTL.
Fairness: FIFO wait queue per path_hmac (max 10 waiters); on release or expiry the next waiter is granted and a server file.lock acquire is sequenced for it.
Lock table in Redis with atomic Lua/SET-NX semantics and expiry sweep emitting file.lock {action:'expire'}; locks released automatically when the owning agent exits or its member leaves/is kicked.
Per-session cap (500 locks) and per-agent cap (100 locks).
conflict hints: when a deny occurs, offer holder agent id to the conflict signaller (B061) through a port.
scope_out: Computing path_hmac (client; BLAKE2b-MAC with the epoch path key).
Enforcing locks on the file system (locks are advisory).
build_against: Redis abstraction in-memory implementation from B009, FakeSequencer/Fanout, injected clock; fixtures contracts/fixtures/events/file.lock*.json.
interfaces: LockService.handle(ctx, frame: FileLockFrameIn): Promise<LockOutcome>  // outcome: granted | denied{holder: agt_} | queued{position} | released | ignored
Redis keys: lock:{sid}:{path_hmac} -> {agent, member, expires_at}; lockq:{sid}:{path_hmac} list; TTL = ttl_ms
acceptance: Two agents acquire the same path_hmac concurrently (100 trials, interleaved): exactly one gets acquire, the other gets a sequenced deny with the holder's agent_id in no field beyond agent_id.
A lock with ttl_ms 5 000 expires at 5 000 ms (fake clock): sweep emits exactly one file.lock expire frame and the path is free; ttl_ms 999 or 600 001 is clamped to 1 000 / 600 000.
Release by a non-owner is ignored and does not free the lock; release by owner frees it and grants the first waiter within the same sequencing step.
Waiters are granted FIFO; the 11th waiter for a path receives deny; the 501st lock in a session is denied.
When agent.exit arrives for an agent holding 3 locks, all 3 are released and 3 expire/release frames are sequenced; same on member kick.
Re-acquire by the holder extends the expiry and emits no deny; re-acquire by the holder of an already-held lock is idempotent for the same frame id.
Only path_hmac matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ and length <= 64 is accepted; the service never receives or stores p.path (inside ct), verified by a test that scans Redis keys and values.
tests: locks.arbitration.test.ts: race and fairness, property test with random interleavings
guardrails: MUST arbitrate on the hash only; MUST NOT read, derive or log `ct.path`.
MUST make acquire atomic (single Redis script or SET NX PX) so no two holders can exist.
MUST NOT block any frame processing waiting for a lock; denial is immediate.
Locks are advisory: MUST NOT reject non-lock frames because of lock state.
A lock MUST be released when its owner can no longer act (agent exit, member left, session ended).
failure_modes: Redis down -> acquire returns deny-by-unavailable (503-class sys.error) rather than granting unsynchronised locks.
Sweep missed (process pause) -> lock TTL in Redis still expires keys; next sweep reconciles by emitting expire for locks it can still see in the index.
Duplicate file.lock frame (same sid, from, id) -> same outcome replayed, no double waiter entry.
